extracted.intended_audience: holders/applicants of trademarks and industrial designs, IP offices, customs authorities, judges and IP practitioners in Member States (Bangui Agreement / OAPI context)
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards and procedural requirements for registration, enforcement and remedies for trademarks and industrial designs under the Annex to the Bangui Agreement (OAPI). Covers acts prior to registration, counterfeiting, interim measures, seizures, border measures, penalties, and industrial design filing/examination/ownership rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts prior to registration not prejudicial
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts prior to the publication of the application for registration of the mark may not be considered to have been prejudicial to the rights attaching thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, acts subsequent to the notification to the alleged counterfeiter of an official copy of the application may be recorded and prosecuted; the competent domestic court shall hold its ruling in abeyance until the registration is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of counterfeiting and liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any infringement of the rights of the owner of the mark as defined in Article 6 shall constitute counterfeiting; counterfeiters shall incur civil and criminal liability for their acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterfeiting may be proven by any means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to seek urgent preventive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person with locus standi to bring action for counterfeiting may make an urgent application to the competent domestic court seeking measures to prevent imminent infringement or continuation of alleged counterfeiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may apply against the alleged counterfeiter or intermediaries whose services are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte / non-inter partes urgent measures standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may order urgent measures on application where circumstances require measures not be taken inter partes, particularly where delay is likely to cause irreparable harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sought ex parte, the court may only order measures if the evidence reasonably accessible to the applicant makes it likely that his rights are being infringed or that such infringement is imminent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available interim remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may prohibit continuation of alleged counterfeiting, subject acts to guarantees to secure compensation, or order seizure or transfer to a third party of suspected infringing products to prevent their introduction into commercial channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures intended to prevent imminent infringement or continuation of alleged counterfeiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may condition measures on guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of urgent or ex parte application, the court may make ordered measures contingent on provision of guarantees by the applicant to compensate the defendant if proceedings are later found without merit or measures cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees are means to protect defendant against unjustified interim measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to commence proceedings after interim measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where measures to stop an infringement are ordered prior to proceedings on the merits, the applicant must file an application, before a civil or criminal court, within 10 working days after the day on which the measure is implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no proceedings are instituted within 10 days, on defendant’s application the interim measures shall be cancelled without prejudice to damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure request and inventory procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a mark or holder of exclusive exploitation rights may request any bailiff, public officer or judicial officer (assisted if applicable by an expert) to make a detailed inventory, with or without seizure, of products claimed to be infringing, following an order by the presiding judge of the competent domestic court, including at the border.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order must specify jurisdiction; inventory/seizure may occur at border.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of registration required for seizure order
rubrics_metrics.description: The order for seizure shall be made on application and on submission of proof of registration of the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit registration proof when seeking seizure orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security deposit for seizure proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where grounds for seizure exist, the order may require the applicant to make a security deposit before the seizure is effected; the deposit shall be adequate without deterring applicants from availing themselves of the procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The security deposit shall always be required of foreigners seeking a seizure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of order to person in possession
rubrics_metrics.description: The person in possession of the objects identified or seized shall be given a copy of the order and, where appropriate, of the document attesting the deposit of security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide such copies exposes the bailiff, public officer or judicial officer and customs official to invalidity and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure void if proceedings not instituted
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the petitioner fail to institute criminal or civil proceedings within 10 working days of the seizure or inventory, such seizure or inventory shall ipso jure be void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voidness is without prejudice to any damages that may be claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court power to order disclosure/search for information
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent domestic court may order, if necessary under financial compulsion, disclosure of all documentation or information held by the defendant or any person in possession of counterfeit products or applying counterfeit processes, for purposes of determining origin and distribution networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure may be ordered if there is no legitimate impediment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of damages criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The court seized shall determine the amount of damages having regard to adverse financial effects, including loss of earnings, suffered by the prejudiced party, the profit made by the counterfeiter and the moral damage caused to the owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court considers both economic loss and moral prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-conviction remedies and publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: On conviction for counterfeiting, the court may order goods found counterfeit and materials/instruments used for their creation be withdrawn from commercial channels, removed, destroyed or confiscated, and may order publicity measures for the verdict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures (withdrawal, destruction, publicity) are ordered to the cost of the counterfeiter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil limitation period for counterfeiting actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil proceedings for counterfeiting are time-barred after five years with effect from the date of the alleged acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five-year limitation applies to civil claims under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for illicit exploitation of a registered mark (enumerated acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified acts are punishable by a fine of 5,000,000 to 30,000,000 CFA francs and imprisonment for three months to two years, or one of these penalties alone; punishable acts include: (a) fraudulent reproduction of a mark (even with added words); (b) knowingly selling or offering for sale goods bearing a counterfeit or fraudulently affixed mark; (c) fraudulently deleting or modifying a properly affixed mark; (d) reproducing/imitating marks likely to create confusion or for similar/identical goods; (e) selling goods bearing fraudulently imitated marks or indications misleading as to nature; (f) fraudulently exploiting a mark for goods marketed by the owner whose state has been modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph details examples of illicit exploitation; penalties specified are numerical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional penalized acts (other exploitative behaviors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Also punishable: (a) knowingly providing a product or service other than that requested under a registered mark; (b) using a mark bearing information liable to mislead the buyer as to the nature of the goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These acts carry the same penalties as illicit exploitation in Article 57.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for failure to affix compulsory marks and use of prohibited signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who (a) do not affix compulsory marks, (b) sell goods that do not bear a compulsory mark, (c) violate terms of decisions under Article 1 of this Annex, or (d) incorporate prohibited signs in their marks shall be punished by a fine of 5,000,000 to 10,000,000 CFA francs and imprisonment for 15 days to six months, or one penalty alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides sanctions specific to compulsory marks and prohibited signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-cumulative penalties rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties specified in Articles 57 and 58 shall not be cumulative; the most severe penalty alone shall be imposed for all acts prior to the first act prosecuted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents stacking of multiple penalties for the same sequence of prior acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recidivism increases penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of recidivism, the penalties specified in Articles 57 and 58 shall be doubled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recidivism is deemed to have occurred where the offender has been convicted of one of the offenses in this Annex within the preceding five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating and aggravating circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of national legislation on mitigating or aggravating circumstances apply to the offenses provided for in this Annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic law governs sentencing adjustments for factors that mitigate or aggravate culpability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprivation of professional electoral rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons convicted of illicit exploitation of a mark may also be deprived of the right to participate in elections to professional groups (e.g., chambers of commerce) for up to 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may order posting/publication of the judgment in specified places and newspapers at the convicted person's cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confiscation and destruction of counterfeited marks/goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may order confiscation of goods bearing marks contrary to Article 59 and of implements/tools used in commission of the offense; court may in all cases order destruction of goods bearing violative marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confiscation may be ordered even in event of acquittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory marks: mandatory measures after violation
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases under Article 58, the competent domestic court shall always order that the marks declared compulsory be affixed to the relevant goods; the court may order confiscation of goods if accused convicted of Article 58 offense during preceding five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affixing compulsory marks is enforceable by judicial order; repeat offenders face confiscation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties applicable to collective and collective certification marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties under Articles 57, 58, 60, 62, 63 and 64 apply to collective marks or collective certification marks; additionally punishable are (a) knowingly using collective marks other than under conditions specified in regulations; (b) selling goods bearing unlawfully used collective marks; (c) using mark reproducing/imitating collective mark within 10 years of forfeiture; (d) selling/providing goods under reproductions/imitation within ten years of invalidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective marks receive the same enforcement regime plus specific prohibitions tied to regulations and forfeiture periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs detention on written application
rubrics_metrics.description: On written application by the owner of a registered mark or beneficiary of an exclusive right, supported by documentary proof, customs administration may detain goods suspected to be counterfeit during inspections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs must immediately inform public prosecutor, applicant and importer, and communicate type and actual/estimated quantity to the rights holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detention lifting timelines and required proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Detention shall be lifted ipso jure within 10 working days, or within three working days for perishable commodities, of notification of detention if applicant fails to provide proof to customs of either (a) interim measures ordered by court; or (b) an application to the competent national judge (civil or criminal) with requisite guarantees to compensate the holder of the goods if alleged counterfeiting ultimately not found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must move promptly to provide judicial protection or interim orders; perishables have shorter timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs may disclose sender/importer info and optional security deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of taking legal action, the applicant may request customs provide names and addresses of sender, importer, quantity and intended recipient of detained goods notwithstanding professional secrecy provisions; on expiry of 10-day limit, owner/importer/recipient may, on payment of a security deposit, cause suspension of detention order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance between investigative needs and confidentiality; deposit allows release pending judicial decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio customs detention and liability
rubrics_metrics.description: In absence of written application, customs authorities may detain goods likely to infringe a registered mark as part of inspection; such detention must be immediately notified to owner and beneficiary and public prosecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customs may incur liability for unjustified detention unless they acted in good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of industrial design and model
rubrics_metrics.description: Any arrangement of lines or colors is a design, and any three-dimensional shape, whether or not associated with lines or colors, is a model, provided it gives a special appearance to an industrial or craft product and may serve as a pattern for manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers 2D and 3D appearances; requirement is special appearance and capability to serve as a pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual protection exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If an object can be considered both a new design and a patentable invention and the elements constituting the novelty of the design are inseparable from those of the invention, the object may only be protected under Patents (Annex I) or Utility Models (Annex II).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents overlapping design and patent protection where novel elements are inseparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design does not exclude other rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection under this Annex does not exclude rights deriving from other legislative provisions of Member States, particularly literary and artistic property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design protection coexists with copyright and other IP rights where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty requirement for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial design may be registered if it is new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty defined as not disclosed anywhere in the world by publication in tangible form, by use or by any other means before the filing date or priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited exceptions to novelty denial (12-month grace)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty shall not be denied if, during the 12 months preceding the filing date, the design was disclosed resulting from (a) manifest abuse in relation to applicant or predecessor, or (b) display by applicant at an official or officially recognized international exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are narrow exceptions allowing limited pre-filing disclosures without destroying novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy/morality exclusion for designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial designs whose exploitation is contrary to public policy or morality may not be registered; commercial exploitation is not considered contrary to public policy or morality merely on account of being prohibited by a legal or regulatory provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application may be refused on public policy/morality grounds with a narrow interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by registration of designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Creator and successors have exclusive right to exploit the design and to sell goods incorporating it for industrial or commercial purposes, subject to Annex conditions and without prejudice to other legal provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive exploitation rights are central benefit of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership presumption and requirement of deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Only properly deposited designs enjoy benefits; design owned by creator or successors, but in absence of proof first applicant presumed to be creator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes importance of timely and proper deposit; first-to-file presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership default rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Jointly created designs yield joint ownership; default rules cover exploitation, compensation, litigation between joint owners, licensing, assignment, right of first refusal, relinquishment and judicial price-fixing where no agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed governance: (a) individual exploitation requires fair compensation to others; (b) proceedings between joint owners must notify others and rulings held in abeyance until notification proof; (c) non-exclusive licenses allowed with compensation and notification; (d) exclusive licenses require agreement of all or court leave; (e) assignments trigger right of first refusal and court-fixed prices; (f) relinquishment entered in registry releases transferor from obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee-created designs: employer vs employee rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Where creator is employee: (a) creations in performance of employment tasks corresponding to actual functions or expressly assigned studies/research belong to employer with supplementary remuneration to employee; (b) creations by employees not contractually required but using company techniques/means/info may give employer ownership or some rights with fair price to employee; (c) other creations belong to employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remuneration and ownership disputes can be fixed by competent domestic court considering contributions and industrial/commercial utility; applies to state/public corporation employees; employer may renounce rights; contractual arrangements must be in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of employee and employer regarding creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employee must immediately inform employer of creation and both must share useful information and refrain from disclosure that may jeopardize exercise of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory communication and confidentiality obligations aim to protect registrability and rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs made to order: default client ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless contract provides otherwise, right to certificate for an industrial design created in fulfillment of an order shall belong to the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties can contract differently, but default rule favors client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exceptions to design rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Design rights do not extend to: (a) acts by person who already owned design on filing date (may use design in their business), (b) acts concerning objects offered for sale in territory by owner or with his consent, (c) private/non-commercial use, (d) reproduction for illustration or education provided not prejudicial to normal exploitation and stating registration and owner's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists common limitations balancing owner rights and prior users/educational uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing contents required
rubrics_metrics.description: Application filed with Organization or Ministry must include: (a) application to Director-General, (b) proof of fee payment, (c) unstamped private power of attorney if represented, (d) statement of product type, (e) two identical copies of graphical/photographic representation or specimen in sealed envelope per measurements (on pain of invalidity), (f) description if necessary, (g) priority document if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict formality: graphical representations in sealed envelope on pain of invalidity; many mandatory elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-design filing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: One filing may include one to 100 designs numbered first to last provided they belong to same Locarno class; designs additional to the hundredth shall not be considered validly deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages bundling similar designs but caps at 100 per filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred publication option
rubrics_metrics.description: At time of filing, applicant may request delayed publication of the design once registered for up to 12 months following the filing date or priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows confidentiality of newly-filed designs for limited period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim formalities and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim priority from earlier application, applicant must file application within six months of prior claim and attach a written declaration and certified true copy of earlier application within three months of filing; multiple priorities require fees and proof for each; late claims beyond three months entail loss of priority though restoration possible under Article 21 and decisions appealable to High Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timing and documentary requirements for claiming priority; restoration possible but subject to procedure and appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report of filing and transmittal timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization or Ministry prepares a report noting filing date/time; copy issued to applicant; Ministry shall transmit documents to Organization within five working days of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative timeline for recordkeeping and transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility criteria for filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date is granted as date of receipt provided application contains: (a) information establishing applicant identity, (b) graphical/photographic representations, (c) products in which designs are incorporated, and (d) proof of payment of prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing required elements may affect filing date/admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication contents for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization shall publish for each application: application number, filing date, graphical/photographic representations, products, applicant name and address, priority claimed, and agent name/address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication ensures transparency and enables oppositions/third-party awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may oppose registration within three months of publication by sending a written statement of reasons based on infringement of Articles 1,2,4 or a prior right, or on a prior filing/priority; Organization sends copy to applicant who may reply within three months (renewable once); Organization may hear parties; its ruling appealable to High Commission within 60 days; Organization may only reject if opposition well-founded; final rejection published in Official Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets strict timelines for opposition and reply, possibility of hearing, appeal path and publication of final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A person not entitled to register who filed an application may be contested; entitled person may claim ownership within three months of publication by written notice; applicant may reply within three months (renewable once); hearing on request; Organization's ruling appealable to High Commission within 60 days; Organization may transfer application only if claim well-founded and final decision published in special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallel administrative procedure to resolve entitlement disputes before registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division (divisional applications) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial application with several designs may be divided into several divisional applications at least until decision on registration, during opposition/claim of ownership proceedings, and during appellate proceedings; divisional apps retain filing and priority dates and require a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows procedural flexibility while preserving priority/filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of formalities and correction of defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization shall examine applications to determine whether formal conditions and fees are met; defective applications (failure to meet Article 8 except 1(b), and Article 9) are notified for remedy within three months (extendable 30 days); remedied application retains original filing date; failure to rectify leads to rejection (issued by Director-General).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection cannot be issued without invitation to correct according to prescribed forms; Organization may correct obvious clerical errors; appeals against rejection within 60 days to High Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal date of registration and issuance of certificate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal date of registration is the filing date; once registration is completed owner is issued a certificate containing registration number, filing number, filing date, Locarno class, products, owner name/address, and validly claimed priority; Organization shall attach graphical/photographic representations to the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate formalizes rights and includes representations for clarity of scope.
